newsitem.title: UK: No let up in sight for European freeze - forecaster.
newsitem.headline: No let up in sight for European freeze - forecaster.

text.p: Europe's New Year freeze is set to continue until at least early next week with temperatures likely to remain below normal for this time of year over the next six to 10 days, a private weather service said on Friday.
"A severe cold wave continues as the predominant wind flow is from the east. Energy demand has been and will continue to be well above normal," said U.S. Weather Services Corp (WSC).
Temperatures over the past 24 hours had averaged 15-30 degrees Fahrenheit (8-15 degrees Celsius) below normal in Northwest Europe, WSC said.
The company said Northwest European temperatures over the next 48 hours would moderate slightly but remain 6-14F (3-7C) below normal on western coasts and 15-25F (8-13C) below normal further east.
Temperatures would average "below to well below normal" from Sunday to Tuesday with a 6-10 day outlook for temperatures to stay below normal, WSC said.
The company did not provide a forecast beyond 10 days.
In Northeast Europe there would be a brief break over the next couple of days in the severe cold but the outlook for the next six to 10 days was for temperatures to remain below normal.
